title: What Pop-Up Cities Is
definition: Pop-Up Cities: cities that assemble for seasons then pack away.
description:
Pop-Up Cities is cities that assemble for seasons then pack away. It sits squarely in Future Cities & Habitats, the frontier where tent districts science becomes flatbed transit infrastructure.

The stakes are folding blocks-scale. Societies that master popup hulls early will shape rapid utilities practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why tent districts programs worldwide now treat Pop-Up Cities as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Pop-Up Cities needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Pop-Up Cities
definition: Today's documented research behind Pop-Up Cities.
description:
The road to Pop-Up Cities is already being paved. Singapore's Smart Nation program instruments the whole city-state with sensors and a national digital twin. Sidewalk Labs' Quayside (Toronto) piloted sensor-rich urban design before its 2020 cancellation.

UN-Habitat projects 68% of humanity will live in cities by 2050, driving urban innovation research. Together these programs form the tent districts foundation that Pop-Up Cities will build on — the flatbed transit results, the rapid utilities methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as flatbed transit research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: The popup hulls Grid
definition: The popup hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Pop-Up Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one tent districts grid that the popup hulls district runs on.

In the Pop-Up Cities architecture, the popup hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the popup hulls fails outright — Pop-Up Cities stops being Pop-Up Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Pop-Up Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first popup hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first popup hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Pop-Up Cities roadmap.
description:
The first popup hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its tent districts grid and flatbed transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the tent districts results have to replicate outside the lab, flatbed transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and rapid utilities operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed tent districts demonstrations, flatbed transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting rapid utilities uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

Depends on: tent districts, flatbed transit, rapid utilities.

title: Readiness Estimator: Pop-Up Cities
definition: Estimates Pop-Up Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Pop-Up Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a popup hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Pop-Up Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Pop-Up Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Pop-Up Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 75641 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where tent districts monitoring, flatbed transit redundancy, or rapid utilities maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Pop-Up Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Pop-Up Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Pop-Up Cities — cities that assemble for seasons then pack away.

Phase 1 — Prove (tent districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (flatbed transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (rapid utilities): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (folding blocks): popup hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and plains-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
